title: The dth Fitting ideal detects smoothness in a pure-dimensional flat family
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is equidimensional of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Write $\Omega^1_{T/B}$ for the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Let $Z_d\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$: on an affine chart with generators $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n$ of the differential module and relation module $K\subset A^n$, this is the ideal generated by the $(n-d)\times(n-d)$ minors of matrices with rows in $K$; for $d\geq n$ it is the unit ideal. These ideals do not depend on the chosen generators and commute with localization [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so they glue to the ideal sheaf $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$; for $d=1$ this is [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the locus $V\subseteq T$ of points $x$ at which $g$ is smooth, i.e. having an open neighbourhood $U$ with $g|_U$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], is open, and $|Z_d|=|T|\setminus V$.

source.place: Tag 0C3K (lemma-d-fitting-ideal-omega-smooth); geometric-fibre formulation using Algebra Tag 00P4 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension) to identify the pure fibre dimension; Fitting convention from More on Algebra Tags 07Z8 and 07ZA

proof.text: A finitely presented algebra is finitely generated: its presentation generators map to algebra generators. Thus local finite presentation of $g$ implies local finite type. Apply the quasi-coherence assertion and the locally-finite-type clause of [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] with $f=g$: $\Omega^1_{T/B}$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module. Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally] with $S=T$, $\mathcal F=\Omega^1_{T/B}$ and $r=d$. For every $x\in T$, $x\notin|Z_d|$ if and only if $\Omega^1_{T/B,x}$ is generated by at most $d$ elements. Put $W=|T|\setminus|Z_d|$; it is open since $Z_d$ is closed.

source.place: Tags 0C3F (lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally) and 05P8 (lemma-locally-free-rank-r-pullback), with More on Algebra Tag 07ZC (lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally), (1) iff (3), for stalk generation; Morphisms Tag 01V2 (lemma-finite-type-differentials) and the quasi-coherence paragraph before Tag 08S2 for the cited differential-sheaf assertions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension] to $g$ and $d$. To match its algebraic-closure-independent hypothesis, choose an algebra equivalence from the standard algebraic closure of each residue field to an arbitrary algebraic closure. Applying Spec and pullback gives an isomorphism of the two geometric fibres; pullback pasting identifies the iterated base change of the ordinary fibre with the direct pullback in the hypothesis. Homeomorphisms identify irreducible components and their dimensions, so the assumed purity transports across this isomorphism, including empty fibres. The final clause of the cited theorem gives $\dim_x(T_{g(x)})=d$ for every $x$. No flatness is used in this step.

source.place: Tag 0C3K hypothesis (3) in its geometric-fibre form, with Varieties Tag 0A21 (3),(5) for the pointwise dimension and Algebra Tag 00P4 for the field extension

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-differential-criterion] to $g$ at $x$. Its stalk map is flat by Flat.stalkMap and [def-weil-flat-morphism], and Step 2 identifies the fibre dimension with $d$. A spanning family indexed by Fin d satisfies the dimension bound. Conversely, the criterion gives a family indexed by Fin n with $n\le d$; extend it along the injection Fin n into Fin d by zero. Its range contains the original spanning family, so it still spans. Thus smoothness at $x$ is equivalent to generation by a Fin d family.

source.place: Tag 01V9, equivalence (1) and (3), applied with the dimension from Step 2

proof.text: Take $V$ to be the complement of the closed support of the dth Fitting ideal. Steps 1 and 3 give the required pointwise characterization, and its openness and the support-complement identity follow from closedness and elementary set identities. For $d=1$, the affine characterization in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally] makes this ideal satisfy the defining property from [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Apply uniqueness of the first Fitting ideal sheaf; the chosen definition need not be definitionally equal to the general Fitting ideal.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0C3K, assembled in Lean by H4 using the stated differential-sheaf, geometric fibre-dimension, Fitting-generator and pointwise smoothness lemmas; algebraic-closure transport and padding of finite spanning families are proved private helpers.

lean.statement: theorem dthFitting_smoothLocus {T B : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ B) (d : ℕ) [Flat g] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g] (hpure : ∀ b : B, (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (B.residueField b) (AlgebraicClosure (B.residueField b)))) ≫ B.fromSpecResidueField b)).IsPureDimension d) : ∃ V : Set T, IsOpen V ∧ (∀ x : T, x ∈ V ↔ ∃ U : T.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ g)) ∧ ((Scheme.Modules.fittingIdealSheaf g.relativeDifferentials d).support : Set T) = Set.univ \ V ∧ (d = 1 → Scheme.Modules.fittingIdealSheaf g.relativeDifferentials 1 = Scheme.firstFittingIdealSheaf g)
